ruleset.name: CiviKitchen
ruleset.description:
Opinionated phpcs standard for CiviCRM extensions, shipped in the civikitchen image. It is CiviCRM's Drupal base MINUS the doc-comment sniffs that fight modern PHPStan array-shape / generic PHPDocs (which PHPStan validates far more precisely), PLUS reusable footgun sniffs: NoLegacyPageForm (warning on classes extending the QuickForm/Smarty UI bases — new UI belongs in SearchKit/Afform), UseExtensionTs (bare ts() resolves in core's translation domain — extensions must use E::ts()), UseMixinsForStandardHooks (no bespoke managed/menu/settings/entity/angular hooks where standard mixins exist), NoRequiredOnExternalAction (the @required trap — inert until an extension lists its externally reachable actions), MaxFileLength (a per-file line-count cap, default 1000, so a runaway class gets split rather than sailing through every token check) and NameBooleanArguments (a warning on positional TRUE/FALSE literals, which since PHP 8 only need a parameter name to become readable).
Third-party rules are preferred over home-grown ones wherever they exist, and are cherry-picked one by one — a whole foreign standard would fight the Drupal base this is built on. The banned CiviCRM call sites that used to be the NoLegacyCall sniff are now phpstan config (/opt/civikitchen-phpstan-config/civicrm-disallowed.neon), which resolves types and so catches the indirect calls a token matcher never saw.
Use it directly (`phpcs --standard=CiviKitchen` / `cklint`) or reference it from a project phpcs.xml.dist (``) and add project-specific paths, config and sniffs on top — the per-extension layer is always yours.
